column1: #        B = credible but narrower or unedited
# Trust is about accountability, not agreement. A tier-A source can be wrong; the tier says
# Most entries are public Algerian sites; the "Global" section at the end adds a curated 2nd tier of
# world sources in the languages Algerians read, so common non-local queries have real answers. All
# are crawled under the open-web profile: robots.txt is obeyed, we identify ourselves as XustiveBot,
# and there is one request per host at a time. If a site disallows us, it is not crawled — that is
# enforced in code, not by convention.
# Algeria-first is not enforced here (trust is about accountability, not geography). It lives in the
# ranker: any .dz host gets an authority home floor above an unlisted global one. So the global tier
# fills gaps and wins on relevance, while a home site still takes a tie.
# Entry points are sitemaps and feeds where the publisher offers them, because a list the site
# maintains itself beats guessing URLs by following links.

column1: # Tier A throughout: these are the primary source for what they publish, and someone is
# constitutionally answerable for it. Several serve an incomplete TLS chain and are unreachable
# until M2-T04.10 — they are listed anyway, because the list should describe what we intend to
# crawl rather than what happens to work this week.
# Wikipedia in the three languages Algerians read. Tier B rather than A: it is credible and
# heavily used, and nobody is accountable for any single edit.
# Seeded at the Algeria portal rather than the front page. A crawler pointed at ar.wikipedia.org/
# will happily spend a month indexing the encyclopaedia of everything, which is not what this
# NOT LISTED HERE, deliberately, and not an oversight.
#   facebook.com    User-agent: *  Disallow: /     — a total block
#   instagram.com   User-agent: *  Disallow: /     — a total block
# Seeding those would produce exactly zero documents: the crawler reads robots.txt, is refused,
# and skips every URL. The list would look like it covered social media while collecting nothing,
# which is worse than an honest gap.
#   youtube.com     allows watch pages, but they are rendered by JavaScript
# Those two are fetchable and would yield a page shell with no content until headless rendering
# Social content comes through **direct collection** instead — [[ADR-0009]], and M2-T01a/b/c plus
# the per-platform connectors. That is a different pipeline with its own identity, fingerprint and
# signature machinery, and it cannot be reached by adding a line to this file.
# The world's most-used sources, in the languages Algerians actually search: Arabic first, then
# French and English. Tier B: these are edited and accountable, but ranked a step below the home
# A-tier here and below any .dz host on the authority signal, so they answer the queries the local
# corpus cannot without displacing Algerian results on local ones. Seeded at the homepage or the
# language section; the same-host crawl and the global depth limit bound each one.
# Deliberately NOT bulk-seeded: Wikipedia (seeded above at the Algeria portals only), and the
# reference/UGC giants (github, stackoverflow, imdb, reddit) — those are pulled page-by-page by
# query-driven discovery and recognised by the domain-authority list, which is the right tool for
# "index the one relevant page", not "crawl the whole site".
